english.title: Wilfully certify a copy of a section 96(2) document / article to be a true copy knowing it is not
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) wilfully certified

(A)_[a document]_
(B)_[an article]_

to be a true copy of a record made by

(C)_[an authority]_
(D)_[a person designated for the purposes of section 96(2) of the Civil Aviation Act 1982 by regulations made by the Secretary of State]_
(E)_[a person acting under the control of an authority]_
(F)_[a person acting under the control of a person designated for the purposes of Section 96(2) of the Civil Aviation Act 1982 by regulations made by the Secretary of State]_

purporting to show the

(G)_[position of an aircraft at a material time,]_
(H)_[terms or content of a message or signal transmitted to or from an aircraft by the authority or a person acting under the control of the authority,]_
(I)_[terms or content of a message or signal transmitted to or from an aircraft by that person or by a person acting under the control of such a person,]_
(J)_[terms or content of a message or signal transmitted to or from an aircraft by a person acting under the control of a person designated for the purposes of section 96(2) of the Civil Aviation Act 1982 by regulations made by the Secretary of State or by a person acting under the control of such a person]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 96(4) of the Civil Aviation Act 1982.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 3 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
